title: Redwood POC weekly sync - benchmark review vs baseline provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results (latency/throughput) vs customer's baseline provider. Redwood shows throughput improvements with lower p99 latency on 2 model flavors when using KV caching and smart batching. Customer raised questions about long-tail latency, tokenization differences, and data residency. Agreed next steps: share raw logs + benchmark spreadsheet, run extended 99th pct tests, propose Dedicated pricing and security docs.
action_items: Laura Kim: Share updated benchmark spreadsheet and raw logs (due 2026-03-05)
Miguel Torres: Run extended 99th percentile latency sweep with 5k-token prompts and attach kernel traces (due 2026-03-06)
Priya Nair: Send production input distribution CSV and target SLOs (due 2026-03-06)
next_steps: Laura to upload benchmark workbook and raw logs to shared drive by 3/5
Miguel to run long-tail latency run and post results by 3/6
Schedule a security follow-up with Redwood security doc pack if infra looks good (tentative: week of 3/9)
Customer to confirm pilot success criteria and timeline for potential Dedicated commit)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Time: 10:00 PST
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Laura Kim (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Aegis Head of ML), Daniel Brooks (Aegis Infra Lead), Sofia Martinez (Aegis PM)

Summary (auto): weekly POC sync focused on performance benchmarks vs baseline provider.

[00:00] Laura: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick check we got the same agenda as last week - go over the benchmark numbers, call out any regressions, and then tune caching/batching settings.
[00:14] Priya: yeah that sounds good, real quick, we had some exec ask about p99 numbers so we'll focus there too.
[00:22] Miguel: cool, I'll share my screen in a sec; note some of the numbers are from our internal run and some from the baseline logs you sent, there may be tokenization differences.
[00:35] Daniel: yeah we exported logs from VendorX baseline, but the token counts sometimes diverged so watch for that.
[00:48] Laura: flagged, we'll annotate the workbook. ok miguel over to you for the slides and the numbers.
[01:02] Miguel: all right, first slide - baseline workload was 500 concurrent users, prompt mix is 70% short (<256 tokens), 25% medium (256-1k), 5% long (>1k). Our runs were on rtx-a100-equivalent nodes for Redwood hosted. In the head-to-head, Redwood achieved about 1.8x throughput at target p95 compared to the baseline provider for the medium prompt set. p50 was similar.
[01:30] Miguel: p99 is where things get interesting - for medium prompts our p99 improved from ~1.8s on baseline to ~1.2s on Redwood with prefix KV caching enabled. For long prompts the improvement shrinks, sometimes we're parity-ish at p99 due to decoding variability and kernel scheduling.
[01:55] Priya: quick clarifying q: when you say KV cache enabled, is that per user or shared across sim sessions? we need to know eviction policies.
[02:07] Miguel: good q - it's per-session prefix cache in this config, TTL 10 minutes, eviction LRU; we can change to sticky per-user if you have long-lived sessions.
[02:20] Daniel: also curious about warmup - did you do a cold-start run for p99 or warm cache? on VendorX we see big spikes when new tokens show up.
[02:34] Miguel: the runs reported were mixed - we included a warmup phase of 5 minutes before capturing steady-state metrics; we'll re-run a cold-start sweep for the long-tail tests.
[02:45] Laura: there's a note in the workbook about warmup; we'll make it explicit.
[02:50] Sofia: are these numbers for the exact same model weights? there was mention of quantized variants.
[02:58] Miguel: yes, we compared the same base model family, one run with 8-bit quantization and one with fp16. quantized paths gave ~15-20% throughput lift and small p50 latency gains, but p99 can widen slightly for some prompts.
[03:20] Priya: that's consistent with our experience. our main blocker is long-tail p99 - if that spikes users report degraded interactions.
[03:30] Miguel: understood. a couple notes: 1) batching shapes matter - we saw that dynamic batching that respects latency SLO kept p95 low while increasing throughput, 2) kernel selection: our runtime picks different kernels for longer sequences which affects jitter.
[03:48] Daniel: when you say kernel selection, is that something we can control in Dedicated? or is it automated?
[03:56] Miguel: it's automated but tunable. on Dedicated you get more knobs (pin kernels, lock to certain cu versions) and we also give a recommended profile per workload.
[04:10] Priya: security question - any difference in logs/exposure for hosted vs dedicated? we need audit logs and KMS.
[04:18] Laura: hosted gives audit logs and customer-scoped access, but Dedicated or Private gives you full control including KMS/HSM and VPC peering. we'll attach the security pack after the call.
[04:29] Priya: thanks.
[04:33] Miguel: back to latency - i pulled the latency distribution plot, here's p50/p95/p99 across prompt lengths. note the p99 tail correlates with high context length and low cache hit rate. the baseline had fewer cache hits because they didn't enable prefix caching in the same way.
[04:55] Priya: can you quantify cache hit rates? like what percent?
[05:01] Miguel: in our steady-state run for medium prompts hit rate was ~62% which gave the biggest win. for the long prompt cohort hit dropped to ~18%.
[05:12] Sofia: do you have recommendations to improve long-tail hit rates?
[05:18] Miguel: yes - 1) encourage client-side prefix reuse, 2) increase TTL for sessions you know are long-lived, 3) for Dedicated customers we can run a small cache cluster to persist more. also consider model distillation for super-long prompts.
[05:34] Daniel: about throughput numbers - what was RPS for the 1.8x claim?
[05:40] Miguel: for medium prompts at p95 SLO we were at ~180 RPS on Redwood nodes vs ~100 RPS on baseline under the same CPU/GPU allocation. that's the aggregate across 4 nodes in our test harness.
[05:55] Laura: quick interjection - to be clear these are lab runs with similar infra but not identical cloud instance types; we'll add a note.
[06:02] Priya: fair. one concern from infra: scheduling variability when you autoscale, does Redwood re-balance KV state or do we see cold caches?
[06:13] Miguel: by default autoscale will spin new workers and cache is local; we recommend session affinity for low-latency apps or using our shared cache layer in Dedicated.
[06:25] Priya: ok makes sense.
[06:30] [Crosstalk]
[06:34] Miguel: Another point - tokenization mismatch, as mentioned earlier, changed token counts up to ~12% between baseline tokenizer and our tokenizer. we normalized by tokens used in the runs but the customer should pick one canonical tokenizer to avoid surprises.
[06:50] Priya: noted, we'll standardize and re-run a sample.
[06:55] Sofia: any callouts on cost? you mentioned throughput improvements, but what about unit token cost?
[07:02] Laura: early numbers show per-1k-token unit cost is comparable or slightly lower on Redwood given the throughput gains; we'll include cost-normalized throughput in the workbook.
[07:12] Miguel: also quantization profiles reduce vCPU/GPU time which lowers cost further; redwood-optimize suggestions included in the docs.
[07:20] Daniel: we need to see end-to-end latency from our app gateway to token stream, not just model-infer time.
[07:28] Miguel: agreed - the raw logs include end-to-end timings; we'll tag request path times separately.
[07:34] Priya: can you run an A/B where we keep our existing baseline routing and route a subset to Redwood for production-like tests?
[07:43] Laura: yes we can do a canary; typical approach is 5-10% of traffic for a week. for the POC we'll simulate with replay and then do a small production canary if metrics look good.
[07:55] Priya: that would be ideal.
[07:58] Miguel: one more note - we saw a single outlier event where p99 spiked to ~3.8s correlated with a background checkpoint on the node; as part of Dedicated we can schedule maintenance windows to reduce these.
[08:12] Daniel: that's the kind of thing we worry about.
[08:16] Laura: ok time for a quick recap and next steps.
[08:20] Laura: action items - we'll share the workbook and raw logs (Laura), Miguel will run the 99th percentile long-run (Miguel), and Priya will send production distribution (Priya). security pack attached afterwards.
[08:35] Priya: can we get a tentative Dedicated pricing estimate if numbers hold? our finance wants a rough number.
[08:42] Laura: yes i'll include a ballpark committed capacity pricing and a few options for monthly vs annual.
[08:49] Sofia: timeline wise, if the long-tail run looks good and security checks out, we can present to execs in two weeks.
[08:57] Laura: sounds good. thanks everyone, we'll follow up via the shared drive and schedule the security session.
[09:05] Priya: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker split and minor word confusions (e.g., "KV cash" vs "KV cache", "VendorX" sometimes transcribed as "Vender X").
